observations.content: Assistant fixed a bug in the cost sim: OBS_PER_M was being applied to a ledger in raw tokens instead of Mtok, so obs was divided by 1e6 wrong; the ledger was also printed as raw tokens instead of Mtok.

Fixed TCO sim for a 1M raw-token session comparing compactAt 150k vs 250k: main agent glm-5.3 $8.93 vs $9.30 (+4%), observer deepseek $0.157 vs $0.133 (-15%), consolidator MiniMax $1.40 vs $1.18 (-15%), rework after amnesia $0.18 vs $0.07 (-60%), TOTAL TCO $10.66 vs $10.69 (dead even, +0%).

Sim showed 150k gives 10 compactions vs 4 at 250k; ledger 1.34M vs 1.14M tokens; 250k burns fewer tokens on compact calls (920k vs 1400k) and fewer observer/consolidator units across all 3 subscription plans.

Assistant concluded 250k threshold beats 150k on 8/10 criteria (zombie dice 7 vs 3, compactions stalls 10 vs 4, working memory 105k vs 153k +45%, rework rounds, error hops, disk) with bill tied; only latency and quality-risk criteria favor 150k.

Assistant identified consolidator (MiniMax, $1.18-1.40, ~13% of TCO and ~90% of OM cost) as the real cost lever, noting switching to glm-5.3-flash could cut it ~10x since flash is ~19x cheaper by input than MiniMax.
Observer timeline: observer summarized ~10.0k tok, produced 17 observations, cost $0.0013, session $0.47 (47 runs).
Consolidator timeline: merged 95 observations into topics, cost $0.1611, session $0.64 (48 runs).
User asked what happens if context is pushed much higher than 250k, e.g. 300k, 500k, 700k, noting cache is not always used, and asked how to evaluate that quality risk.
Compaction counts by threshold: 150k=9, 250k=4, 300k=3, 500k=2, 700k=1; a single cache miss at 700k costs $0.98 and expired cache during idles/subagents re-prefills from scratch.

Assistant derived law: higher threshold means more sensitivity to cache hit rate (90% to 30% hit raises bill +65% at 150k but +133% at 700k); 500k/700k never win on cost at any hit rate; 250k stays the sweet spot (+3-19% vs 150k).

Web research found Z.ai GLM Coding Plan: all tiers (Lite/Pro/Max) support up to 1M context but you must append [1m] suffix to the model name (e.g. glm-5.3[1m]); without suffix the default is 200k — models.json id is zaicp/glm-5.3 with NO suffix, so anything above 200k may silently truncate or error.
Research also found GLM-5.3 coding plan has mandatory thinking, 1M text-only context with 128K output, and endpoint api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4.

Assistant proposed a 4-tier quality-risk evaluation protocol: 1 truncation probe (~$0.30), 2 needle-recall curve (~$2-3), 3 instruction-drift (~$1), 4 real-work A/B telemetry (free, slowest); noted if 200k is the real cap the options are adding [1m] to models.json id or lowering compactAt to 180k.
User approved running the evaluation, saying 'thử xem nào? đánh giá đi nhé'.

Assistant built a combined probe: a ~247k-token filler document (989,346 chars, N=1300 blocks) with head marker MAGIC-START-7F3A, needles at ~25/50/75/90/98% depth (NEEDLE-ALPHA-25/0325, BRAVO-50/0650, CHARLIE-75/0975, DELTA-90/1170, ECHO-98/1274), and an instruction-drift rule in system prompt requiring every reply to begin with the word PINECONE; cost estimate ~$0.7 total by reusing cached prefix.

Probe results via cli-proxy-api:8317 for model zaicp/glm-5.3: all three queries billed only 180,005/180,012/180,004 prompt tokens with 0 cached tokens (not the ~247k sent), the head marker MAGIC-START-7F3A was recalled correctly, all 5 needle codes were listed, last block reported as 1299, and every reply began with PINECONE (no instruction drift).
